hints: Focus on what each role looks like, acid means donating $H^+$ to make a new acid, oxidising means the sulfuric acid itself gets reduced to $SO_2$.
Remember the halide trend, $HCl$ from chlorides is not oxidised further, but $HBr$ from bromides is oxidised to brown $Br_2$.
Look for the compound that first gives its own $H$-containing product and then has that product oxidised by a second molecule of concentrated acid.
walkthrough:
**Separate the two jobs**

Think like a teacher checking two boxes. As a strong acid, concentrated $H_2SO_4$ donates $H^+$ to make $CO_2$, $HCl$, $HBr$, etc. As an oxidising agent, $H_2SO_4$ itself is reduced, usually $S(+VI)$ to $S(+IV)$ in $SO_2$.

$$H_2SO_4 \text{ (acid): gives } H^+ \quad , \quad H_2SO_4 \text{ (oxidant): becomes } SO_2$$

**Test the acid-only cases**

With magnesium carbonate you get fizzing only. With potassium chloride you get steamy white fumes of $HCl$ only.

$$MgCO_3 + H_2SO_4 \rightarrow MgSO_4 + CO_2 + H_2O$$
$$KCl + H_2SO_4 \rightarrow KHSO_4 + HCl$$

**See the double reaction with sodium bromide**

First, the acid step makes $HBr$. Then concentrated $H_2SO_4$ is strong enough to oxidise $HBr$ to brown $Br_2$, and itself forms $SO_2$. That is both roles in one test tube.

$$NaBr + H_2SO_4 \rightarrow NaHSO_4 + HBr \text{ (acid step)}$$
$$2HBr + H_2SO_4 \rightarrow Br_2 + SO_2 + 2H_2O \text{ (oxidising step)}$$

options.A: Incorrect. $MgCO_3$ reacts only as a base with the acid to give $MgSO_4$, $CO_2$ and $H_2O$. There is no change in oxidation number, so $H_2SO_4$ is not acting as an oxidising agent.
options.B: Incorrect. $KCl$ reacts only as an acid-base reaction to give $HCl$ fumes: $KCl + H_2SO_4 \rightarrow KHSO_4 + HCl$. $Cl^-$ is hard to oxidise, so concentrated $H_2SO_4$ cannot oxidise $HCl$ to $Cl_2$ under these conditions.
options.C: Correct. $NaBr$ first undergoes an acid reaction to form $HBr$, then $HBr$ is oxidised by more concentrated $H_2SO_4$ to $Br_2$ with $SO_2$ formed. So $H_2SO_4$ acts both as a strong acid and as an oxidising agent.
options.D: Incorrect. $SO_3$ dissolves in concentrated $H_2SO_4$ to form oleum, $H_2S_2O_7$, with no proton transfer acting as a strong acid on $SO_3$ and no redox. Sulfur is already +VI in both, so no oxidation occurs.
